answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned rate limits: a new identity starts throttled, able to claim only tiny rewards, and its cap grows only after a long trail of verified useful work. Like a trellis guiding a vine upward, the record shapes growth; a zephyr of fresh fake accounts blows past quickly because each clone must redo months of honest work to reach full rates. A vault of escrowed earnings backs the history, so abandoning an aged identity to start fresh costs real income, making mass forgery slow and unprofitable.
